text:
maria: quick sync — final checklist before we surface the new 'calypso-xl-1' model in hosted and dedicated. weights are staged at s3://redwood-models/calypso-xl/2026-03-10/calypso-xl-1-pt.tar.gz (sha256: 3f5a...). tokenizer files are next to that: tokenizer.json + merges.txt.

kevin: thanks — i'll validate weight checksum and run the perf harness later today. any special loading flags?

maria: main runtime flags: `--kv-cache-type=v2`, `--quantize=bf16` for now (we couldn't reproduce int8 perf improvement on A100s). Also set `max_seq_len=4k` in model config. note: model uses a SentencePiece vocab but we exported both `tokenizer.json` (HuggingFace style) and `spm.model`. prefer `spm.model` for exact tokenization parity.

jordan: flagged that in the model metadata PR (#742). quick check: does the hf-style `tokenizer.json` map unknown chars differently? would like to avoid user-facing token drift.

maria: yes — hf json normalizes some unicode sequences; spm.model is canonical for this checkpoint. we'll mark the hf json as "compatibility" only and add a note in docs about the difference and migration tips.

priya: for docs/customer blurb — what capabilities should we highlight and what quirks to call out? thinking short bullets: general-purpose assistant, better long-context coherence >8k, steerable via system prompts. quirks: prefers punctuation for truncation boundaries, edge-case tokenization of emojis (split into multiple tokens).

maria: exactly. draft blurb: "Calypso XL is optimized for long-context instruction-following; best for summarization and multi-turn docs assistant. Known quirks: emoji tokenization fragmentation, and slightly different HF vs SPM tokenization — use `spm.model` for exact parity."

kevin: CI run started: `/ci/run_e2e calypso-xl-1 perf smoke` — tagging @model-ci-bot to echo results.

model-ci-bot: CI: e2e perf smoke for calypso-xl-1 started at 2026-03-17T14:22Z. estimated 12m.

jordan: i kicked off serving validation on a dedicated node (g5x2). memory p95 looks fine, but we saw 1.8% higher latency on prompt-length 2048 compared to baseline. i'll open a tiny config tweak PR to lower `batch_delay_ms` from 6 -> 4.

priya: for the customer-facing name — can we use "Calypso XL" or should we append a capability tier like "Calypso XL (long-context)"? marketing prefers short names but product wants clear capability hint.

maria: let's do "Calypso XL" in the model catalog and add a short tagline: "Calypso XL — long-context generative model (up to 16k tokens)" in the docs page. that matches other entries.

docs-bot: Draft docs page created: https://docs.redwood.ai/models/calypso-xl (internal draft). PR: docs#1194.

kevin: checksum and smoke perf done — weights match, basic generation heuristics pass. leaving detailed perf runs to overnight.

jordan: pushed PR #748 with `batch_delay_ms` tweak + perf-regression guard. can someone review? small change in serving config only.

priya: reviewing now. i'll also draft the customer-facing release note (short list of capabilities + known quirks). will post copy here for a quick ✅ before publishing.

maria: awesome. plan: wait for CI + jordan's tweak to land, then schedule catalog + docs publish tomorrow 10:00 PT, announce in #product + email to early-access customers. if anyone objects to timing shout now. :rocket:

kevin: looks good to me.

jordan: LGTM pending CI.

priya: will post the release note draft in ~30m.

model-ci-bot: CI: e2e perf smoke completed — all checks green. artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/calypso-xl/1763456789/

maria: perfect — thanks all. closing loop here after docs PR merges.

priya: release note (draft):
- Name: Calypso XL
- Short: Long-context generative model, optimized for multi-document summarization and chat over long conversations.
- Highlights: up to 16k tokens, improved coherence on >8k contexts, supports streaming and function-calling.
- Known quirks: emoji tokenization may split into multiple tokens (affects token count); use `spm.model` to match runtime tokenization exactly; avoid heavy integer quantization on current release (we recommend bfloat16).

maria: nice — that's the copy we'll use. thanks everyone.

kevin: ping me if we want to run the latency SLO harness across regions before announce.

maria: will do. end of thread.
